title: The terms of the point-of-sale lesser-price charge and its reach to health benefit plans and PBM contracts
rule_summary: M.G.L. c. 94C, § 21C(a) defines cost-sharing as an amount owed by an individual under the terms of the individual's health benefit plan, a term it takes from M.G.L. c. 176O, § 1, which defines a health benefit plan as a policy, contract, certificate or agreement entered into, offered or issued by a carrier to provide, deliver, arrange for, pay for, or reimburse any of the costs of health care services; and defines the pharmacy retail price as the amount an individual would pay for a prescription drug at a pharmacy if the individual purchased that prescription drug at that pharmacy without using a health benefit plan or any other prescription medication benefit or discount. Section 21C(b) requires a pharmacy, at the point of sale, to charge an individual for a prescription drug the lesser of the applicable cost-sharing amount or the pharmacy retail price. Under § 21C(c) a health benefit plan or carrier shall not require an insured to make a cost-sharing payment for a prescription drug in an amount greater than that charged pursuant to § 21C(b). Under § 21C(d) no contractual obligation between a pharmacy benefit manager, as defined in M.G.L. c. 176Y, § 1, and a pharmacist shall prohibit a pharmacist from complying with the section.
exam_relevance: Tests what the pharmacy retail price is (the price at that pharmacy without a health benefit plan or any other prescription medication benefit or discount), that the plan or carrier may not require a cost-sharing payment greater than the amount the pharmacy charged, and that a PBM contract cannot prohibit the pharmacist from complying.

authority.name: Massachusetts General Laws, point of sale charge for prescription drug and limit on amount of cost-sharing payment

common_confusions: Using a price obtained through a benefit or discount as the pharmacy retail price. The definition is the amount paid at that pharmacy without a health benefit plan or any other prescription medication benefit or discount.
Treating a PBM contract term as authority to collect the higher amount. No contractual obligation between a pharmacy benefit manager and a pharmacist shall prohibit the pharmacist from complying.
Placing the charging duty on the plan. M.G.L. c. 94C, § 21C(b) is a duty of the pharmacy at the point of sale; § 21C(c) separately binds the health benefit plan or carrier.
verification_notes: Read in the current text of M.G.L. c. 94C, § 21C, inserted by section 27 of chapter 342 of the Acts of 2024, and of the health benefit plan definition in M.G.L. c. 176O, § 1, on malegislature.gov on 2026-09-16.
